fr.elements: Main Residence; Front Driveway; Front Entry Area; Open Lawn Area; Patio Area; Walkway; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Street Frontage
fr.considerations: Single Access Point; Dense Vegetation; Dense Vegetation; Limited Turnaround Space; Vegetation Near Structure
fr.recommendations:
• Install a reflective address marker at the driveway entrance visible from both directions of travel on the street.
• Keep the driveway clear of parked vehicles to allow fire apparatus to reach the front entry area.
• Trim vegetation along the driveway edges so a full-width vehicle can pass without obstruction.
• Cut back dense vegetation near the structure to create clear space between plants and exterior walls.
• Mark or designate a flat area on the property where emergency vehicles can turn around, and keep that area clear at all times.

wildfire.conditions: Structure Surrounded by Vegetation; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Tree Cluster; Scattered Trees; Vegetation Near Structure; Vegetation Near Structure; Limited Vegetation Separation; Open Green Space; Single Access Route; Scattered Shrubs; Mixed Vegetation
wildfire.recommendations:
• Remove or thin the dense tree clusters closest to the structure to create more open space between the trees and the building.
• Trim branches from trees that hang directly over or within a few feet of the roof and walls.
• Cut back shrubs and low plants that are growing against or touching the outside walls of the structure.
• Thin the mixed vegetation surrounding the structure to break up the continuous ring of plants and trees pressing close to the building.
• Remove dead or dry material from within the scattered shrubs near the structure.
• Keep the single access route clear of overhanging branches and encroaching vegetation along both sides so vehicles can pass through without obstruction.
• Mark the driveway entry clearly so it remains visible to responding vehicles approaching under low visibility conditions.
• Maintain the open green space by keeping it mowed or grazed short, particularly in areas adjacent to the structure.
• Thin scattered trees near the structure to widen the open areas between the tree canopy and the building walls.
